envelope.text: - `get_child` exists (RFC-0102) with two bounds of its own, stated on it: a

why:
rclcpp's `Logger` is a VALUE type holding a `std::string name_`, copied into every macro call, and `get_child` mints a new one by concatenating `parent.child`. Constraints: no allocator, and no `<string>` on a freestanding C++ build -- `nros-cpp` headers are compiled `-nostdinc++` against Zephyr's minimal libcpp, where the rule (RFC-0018, issue 0112) is to gate a std include on `NROS_CPP_STD` rather than `__STDC_HOSTED__`, because a hosted compiler invoked `-nostdinc++` still reports itself hosted. (`rclcpp/logging.hpp` itself still gates its `<cstdio>` on `defined(NROS_CPP_STD) || (__STDC_HOSTED__ + 0)`; that one is the include 0112 explicitly left on the hosted gate, since minimal libcpp does provide `<cstdio>`.) Ours is an OPAQUE `const void*` returned by `Node::get_logger()` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/node.hpp`), pointing at a `&'static nros_log::Logger` in a bounded 32-slot intern table keyed on `&'static str`. `Logger::Logger` and `Logger::get_child` follow from that: a `void*` has no constructor and no allocator to build a child name with. What does NOT follow is that the accessors are missing -- see `cpp:Logger::get_name` and `cpp:Logger::set_level`. A named `nros::Logger` wrapper over the same handle would cost one struct and restore the type without restoring the allocation.

phase-428 W6 (2026-09-06) — disposition, required because this row's SHAPE CORRESPONDS: the name exists on the ported surface and the correlator files it `same`, so nothing in a build says the contract differs. That is the class RFC-0089 exists for.

FIRST, A CORRECTION to the text above, which says ours is "an OPAQUE `const void*` returned by `Node::get_logger()`". That is no longer the C++ surface. `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/logging.hpp:246` declares a real `class rclcpp::Logger` holding a `const char* name_`, with `explicit Logger(const char* name = "")` and `get_name()`, alongside `rclcpp::get_logger(const char*)` and a `std::string` overload guarded by `NROS_CPP_HAS_STD_STRING`. The `const void*` is still the C spelling (`c:node_get_logger`); the C++ one moved in RFC-0089 stage 6 step A. The allocator argument above still explains why there is no `std::string` member and no `get_child`.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: the logger NAME reaches the output and keys per-logger level configuration; `get_child` mints a sub-logger by concatenation.

OURS: the name is carried and readable via `get_name()`, but the `RCLCPP_*` macros expand to `NROS_*`, which take no logger — the header says so in as many words: "The logger NAME is lost (nros has no per-logger dispatch yet)".

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: `logger.get_child("x")` is a COMPILE ERROR — no such member. The LOST NAME is not loud: a ported `RCLCPP_INFO(rclcpp::get_logger("planner"), ...)` compiles, logs, and attributes the line to nothing. That is the envelope, and it is stated in the header and not only here, which is what ADOPT-BOUNDED requires. `cpp:RCLCPP_FATAL` is the same discard measured on the severity rather than on the name.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ROW CORRECTED to the code. The OURS / HOW A USER FINDS OUT paragraphs above say the `RCLCPP_*` macros expand to `NROS_*`, take no logger, and lose the name, citing the header's "The logger NAME is lost". That stopped being true at phase-417 W3.a (issue 1019): the family routes through `NROS_LOG_*` with the logger's handle, and `rclcpp/logging.hpp` now reads "THE LOGGER IS CARRIED, NOT DISCARDED", so a ported `RCLCPP_INFO(rclcpp::get_logger("planner"), ...)` is attributed to `planner` and honours its level. The `const char*` name in the correction paragraph also no longer lives at `rclcpp/logging.hpp:246`. What remains bounded: no `get_child` (a compile error), and the name is BORROWED, not owned — so whatever `const char*` (or `std::string`, whose `c_str()` the `get_logger(const std::string&)` overload borrows) the Logger was built from must outlive it. Both are now on the class's doc comment, which is the envelope; before this the class had only a `//` banner Doxygen does not render.

issue 1682 (2026-10-05) -- the name is no longer borrowed. `rclcpp::Logger` holds an OWNED `nros::FixedString<NROS_CPP_LOGGER_NAME_CAPACITY + 1>` (default 128 bytes, `MAX_RESOLVED_NAME_LEN`), so `get_name()` survives the string it was built from, as upstream's owned `std::string` does -- `get_logger(node_name + ".planner").get_name()` read freed memory before. A fixed string rather than `std::string` keeps it heap-free and present on freestanding targets; the residual bound is truncation past the capacity, stated on the class. What remains bounded: no `get_child`. Its stated reason ("needs an allocator to build the name in") no longer holds now that the name has inline storage -- it is implementable, and not done here.

phase-479 (2026-10-05) -- LANDED. `get_child` exists (RFC-0102), so the class's remaining bounds are the owned name's truncation past `NROS_CPP_LOGGER_NAME_CAPACITY` (issue 1682) and `get_child`'s own, which its row carries. Envelope moved with the text.
